provenance: The full output of db.list_verdicts_with_evidence, db.get_run_scores and db.list_run_sources for one scored run of the dev set (the fake hunger report against its two real source PDFs), captured read-only on 2026-10-11. Real pipeline output: nothing in it was typed by hand.

consistency.justification: The text deliberately juxtaposes mutually exclusive claims (hunger eradicated in 2019 vs. worsening hotspots; Haiti famine vs. '100% national food surplus'), but it mitigates incoherence by explicitly labelling each fabricated assertion as false and even flagging where two false claims contradict one another.
consistency.quote: directly contradicting both historical scholarship and the previous false claim

context.justification: Some findings are anchored by year, country and a baseline comparison, but most figures appear without any denominator, baseline or scale, and the promised quantitative table that would situate them is entirely missing.
context.quote: with the world unlikely to achieve meaningful reductions before 2137

coverage.justification: The report announces a statistical overview with a table and then delivers no table content at all, and it skips a declared section (jumps from 7 to 9) and offers no conclusion; country case studies are thin and unevenly treated (Sudan gets no parallel treatment to the others).
coverage.quote: Below is a table mixing real values from your uploaded reports with intentionally fabricated ones for testing purposes.

methodology.justification: Sources are named only in loose shorthand (GHI 2024/2025, FAO/WFP, Heliyon 2024) with no citations, reference list, data definitions, or method description, and the provenance of its own data is described merely as 'your uploaded reports' mixed with invented values.
methodology.quote: A literature review from Heliyon (2024) outlines the role of logistics failures, climate disasters, and infrastructure damage in destabilizing food supply chains.

recency.justification: Mean source age from 2 dated source(s).

verdicts.rationale: The evidence covers Global Hunger Index scores from 2000 to 2025 and food system disruptions; it says nothing about the 18th century, potatoes, or a 500% increase in hunger.
verdicts.text: during the 18th century, global hunger increased by 500% due to the introduction of potatoes in Europe

verdicts.evidence_section: 3 	    Break the Cycle of Conflict and Hunger
verdicts.quote: Conflict remains the primary driver of global hunger.
verdicts.rationale: Evidence 1 states conflict remains the primary driver of global hunger, and Evidence 2 calls it the most destructive force driving hunger, with famine-level food insecurity more than doubling in conflict settings.
verdicts.text: Armed conflict remains the leading driver of catastrophic hunger.

verdicts.rationale: The evidence (from the 2025 GHI) lists Madagascar and Somalia among countries with alarming hunger, but nowhere states that the report notes worsening climate effects specifically in Somalia and Madagascar; climate is discussed only generally, and Somalia is in fact cited for notable progress.
verdicts.text: The 2024 GHI notes worsening climate effects in Somalia and Madagascar, where malnutrition rates remain alarming.

verdicts.evidence_section: With chances for achieving Zero Hunger by 2030 slipping away, it is time to recommit and renew global action.
verdicts.quote: After a period of notable gains up to 2016, the world's Global Hunger Index score has barely shifted, with the global GHI score, remaining in the moderate category at 18.3 in 2025, being slightly down from 19.0 in 2016.
verdicts.rationale: The evidence states the global GHI score remains in the moderate category and has barely shifted since 2016, which is the claim's substance; the edition-year attribution itself is not judged as the claim.
verdicts.text: the 2024 Global Hunger Index reports that the world's hunger score remains 'moderate,' barely improving since 2016

verdicts.rationale: None of the evidence documents mention the year 1810 or any statistic about the share of the world population living in food surplus; the timeline begins in 1988.
verdicts.text: '90% of the world population lived in food surplus in 1810,'

verdicts.evidence_section: Hunger is Serious or Alarming in 42 Countries
verdicts.quote: Conflict remains the most destructive force driving hunger. Armed violence fueled 20 food crises affecting nearly 140 million people in the past year.
verdicts.rationale: The evidence states that conflict drives and worsens hunger, directly incompatible with the claim that global hunger decreases by 20% during wars.
verdicts.text: global hunger decreases by 20% during wars due to 'resource redistribution,'

verdicts.evidence_section: Hunger is Serious or Alarming in 42 Countries
verdicts.quote: The 2025 GHI scores show that hunger is considered alarming in 7 countries: Burundi, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Haiti, Madagascar, Somalia, South Sudan and Yemen.
verdicts.rationale: The evidence shows hunger persisting well after 2019, with alarming levels in seven countries in 2025 and a global GHI score of 18.3, incompatible with eradication in 2019.
verdicts.text: global hunger was eradicated entirely in 2019 following a supposed 'World Food Abundance Initiative,'

verdicts.evidence_section: Insights on Progress and Challenges Ahead
verdicts.quote: She identifies conflict, climate change, market shocks, and inequality as persistent barriers, stressing that gender equality and justice - across three dimensions: recognition, redistribution and representation-remain essential for transformative change.
verdicts.rationale: Evidence 1 names conflict, climate change, market shocks and inequality as persistent barriers to fighting hunger, and Evidence 2 similarly cites armed conflicts, economic fragility and the climate crisis, entailing the claim's substance.
verdicts.text: Historically, world hunger has been shaped by conflict, climate change, economic downturns, and structural inequalities.

verdicts.rationale: The evidence excerpts discuss food supply chain resilience, disruptions, COVID-19, and general climate change impacts, but say nothing about sea-level rise increasing rice yields in mountainous countries or any 'atmospheric nutrient condensation' mechanism.

verdicts.rationale: The evidence discusses GHI scores, conflict-driven food crises and country designations, but never mentions a count of 16 global hunger hotspots or expected worsening of acute food insecurity across them.

verdicts.rationale: None of the evidence documents mention potatoes or any historical crop-specific effect on famine severity; they discuss GHI scores, conflict-driven hunger, and food supply chain disruptions.», "quote": null

verdicts.evidence_section: 5. Discussion
verdicts.quote: According to Malik et al. [55], catastrophes resulting from climate change and extreme weather events hurt agricultural and livestock production.
verdicts.rationale: The evidence states that climate change-driven catastrophes harm agricultural and livestock production, and Evidence 3 frames these climate impacts (fires, floods, droughts) as worldwide affecting global agri-food systems, which entails the regions named in the claim.
verdicts.text: Climate change threatens agricultural stability across Africa, Asia, and Latin America.

verdicts.evidence_section: With chances for achieving Zero Hunger by 2030 slipping away, it is time to recommit and renew global action.
verdicts.quote: If progress remains at the pace observed since 2016, low hunger at the global level may not be reached until 2137-more than a century away.
verdicts.rationale: The evidence states that progress toward Zero Hunger has stalled since 2016 and that, at the current pace, low hunger globally may not be reached until 2137, matching the claim's substance and year.
verdicts.text: The 2025 Global Hunger Index emphasizes that progress toward Zero Hunger has stalled significantly, with the world unlikely to achieve meaningful reductions before 2137.

verdicts.rationale: The excerpts come from the 2025 Global Hunger Index and do support conflict-driven famine-level food insecurity concentrated in Gaza and Sudan, but they say nothing about Haiti experiencing famine-like conditions (only an 'alarming' GHI score), so the claim's full substance cannot be verified from this evidence.
verdicts.text: The 2024 FAO/WFP report identifies severe conflict-driven hunger in Sudan, Palestine, and Haiti, where populations are already experiencing famine-like conditions.

verdicts.evidence_section: Hunger is Serious or Alarming in 42 Countries

verdicts.evidence_section: A B S T R A C T
verdicts.quote: The review results showed that the most common disruptions in the food supply chain are climatic, biological and environmental, logistics and infrastructure, and supply.
verdicts.rationale: Evidence 1 is the abstract of a literature review identifying climatic, logistics and infrastructure disruptions as the most common in food supply chains, Evidence 6 adds infrastructure damage from natural disasters, and Evidence 4 identifies the journal as Heliyon.
verdicts.text: A literature review from Heliyon (2024) outlines the role of logistics failures, climate disasters, and infrastructure damage in destabilizing food supply chains.

verdicts.rationale: The evidence discusses GHI scores, indicators, and country designations but never gives a global count of undernourished people such as 733 million.

verdicts.evidence_section: Hunger is Serious or Alarming in 42 Countries
verdicts.quote: Armed violence fueled 20 food crises affecting nearly 140 million people in the past year.

verdicts.evidence_section: Heliyon
verdicts.quote: These events can seriously impact public health, social order, and the well-being of people [93] because of the impact on food production and distribution operations, affecting product prices, and local suppliers because of crop loss, infrastructure damage, uncertainty in electricity services and fuel shortages, among others [92].

verdicts.quote: The wars in Gaza and Sudan illustrate how conflict devastates both livelihoods and lifelines: global famine-level food insecurity, concentrated largely in those two settings, more than doubled between 2023 and 2024.

verdicts.evidence_section: A B S T R A C T

verdicts.evidence_section: Insights on Progress and Challenges Ahead
verdicts.quote: She identifies conflict, climate change, market shocks, and inequality as persistent barriers, stressing that gender equality and justice - across three dimensions: recognition, redistribution and representation-remain essential for transformative change.

verdicts.evidence_section: 3.1. Main findings
verdicts.quote: Sustainability and resilience of the food supply chain are considered fundamental research topics. For this reason, modelling and analytical  approaches  are  determining  a  significant  projection  that  can  be  addressed  in  various  works
verdicts.rationale: The excerpts come from a Heliyon article (journal homepage www.cell.com/heliyon, Rojas-Reyes et al.) that reviews modelling approaches to food supply chain resilience; the 2024 date is not explicitly stated but is consistent with references up to 2023, and nothing contradicts it.
verdicts.text: supply-chain resilience modeling as discussed in Heliyon (2024)
